The image clearly shows green banana fruits with dark brown-to-black lesions at the tips and on the surface of the fruit fingers. The image is labeled "Wound anthracnose" and the text describes symptoms appearing after sea transport/packing. The lesions are characteristic dark, sunken spots typical of anthracnose infection on banana fruit.

**Key visual evidence:**
- **Affected part:** Banana fruit (fingers/tips)
- **Color:** Dark brown to black lesions
- **Pattern:** Discrete, focal dark spots concentrated at fruit tips and wound sites
- **Context:** Post-harvest, post-transport symptoms on green banana fingers
- The label in the image itself reads "Wound anthracnose"

This matches **Anthracnose** — caused by *Colletotrichum musae*, characterized by dark, sunken lesions on banana fruit, especially at wound sites or tips, often appearing after harvest during or after transport.
